defect.evidence_quote: commercial structures which are not used as private residences
defect.problem: The disclosed evidence does not support assigning See to Curtilage. The opinion concerns a locked commercial warehouse and commercial structures, and the only disclosed occurrence of Curtilage is the page's asserted front-matter home entry.
defect.proposed_fix: Remove the Curtilage home role unless the corpus discloses a separate taxonomy/source note explaining the cross-doctrine curtilage connection.

reasons: The full opinion text contains no curtilage reference.
The opinion frames the issue as commercial inspections, not the home-curtilage boundary.
residual_risks: A separate Curtilage page or taxonomy note might justify this cross-link, but it is not in the disclosed files.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Do not route this case to Curtilage on the disclosed record.

defect.evidence_quote: The businessman, like the occupant of a residence, has a constitutional right to go about his business free from unreasonable official entries upon his private commercial property.
defect.problem: The holding is substantively supported, but the phrase homeowner is a loose paraphrase of the opinion's occupant of a residence language and could be read too narrowly.
defect.proposed_fix: Change homeowner to occupant of a residence.

reasons: The warrant-rule portion is directly supported by the opinion's statement that nonconsensual administrative entry on nonpublic commercial premises may be compelled only within a warrant procedure.
The refusal/punishment portion is supported by the opinion's statement that appellant may not be prosecuted for insisting that the fire inspector obtain a warrant.
residual_risks: The opinion itself notes licensing programs and other regulatory settings, so the word generally is important and should remain.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use: An administrative inspection of the nonpublic portions of commercial premises generally requires a warrant; a businessman, like the occupant of a residence, may refuse a warrantless regulatory entry and cannot be punished for that refusal.

reasons: The opinion repeatedly describes administrative entry and inspection of commercial property by regulatory officials.
The asserted role Anchor (commercial inspections) matches the case's actual issue: warrantless administrative inspection of nonpublic commercial premises.
residual_risks: No separate Special Needs and Administrative Searches page is disclosed, so only the commercial-administrative-search fit is verified.

residual_risks: Treatment correctness is reserved for Lens B.
